summary: We fixed a problem with monitoring rover on Mars.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

ALIAN TEAM — Mars Mission Control is a web-based, cinematic aerospace operations console and interactive 3D telemetry portal designed to explore Martian flight, surface, orbital, and deep-space missions.

How it works:

  • Full-Stack Monorepo Architecture: Built as a decoupled system featuring a Next.js 14 frontend (apps/web) communicating with a high-performance Fastify backend API (apps/server) backed by an embedded SQLite (better-sqlite3) database.
    • Mission Control (control): Displays real-time telemetry (temperatures, atmospheric pressure, wind velocity, dust opacity, battery metrics, signal latency, and communication relays).
    • Interactive Mars Globe (globe): A GPU-accelerated 3D planetary viewer built with Three.js / React Three Fiber showing accurate Martian topographic landing sites, coordinates, and vehicle locations.
    • Hazard Scanner (scanner): Evaluates surface and atmospheric environmental risks (radiation, terrain obstacles, extreme dust storm opacity).
    • ISRU Vault (vault): Manages In-Situ Resource Utilization metrics and landing zone resource potentials.
    1. Terrain slope & surface roughness
    2. Atmospheric weather conditions
    3. Radiation shielding levels
    4. Local resource availability (ISRU)
  • Telemetry & NASA API Integration: Pulls Mars Weather, telemetry, and camera imagery from NASA APIs with automatic fallback caching and simulated telemetry generation to guarantee seamless operation under offline conditions or rate limits (HTTP 429).
  • Mission Log System: Role-based event logging with persistent storage in SQLite, secured via RS256 / JWT authentication.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Unified Historical & Live Analytics: Consolidates data from pioneering historical missions and modern systems (including Sojourner, Spirit & Opportunity, Viking Landers, Phoenix & InSight, Dawn, NEAR Shoemaker, Pioneer 10 & 11, Ingenuity, and Kepler) into a single operational interface.
  • Zero Downtime / High Fault Tolerance: Implements graceful degradation—if NASA APIs experience timeouts, errors, or rate limits, the system provides real-time fallback telemetry without breaking the UI.
  • High Performance (60 FPS): Engineered to eliminate layout thrashing by syncing smooth scrolling (Lenis) with GSAP Ticker and lazy-loading 3D WebGL canvases with Server-Side Rendering bypass (ssr: false).
  • Operator Usability: High-contrast aerospace telemetry styling with instant keyboard/magnetic controls, audio feedback via Howler.js, and clear status indicators (battery level, DSN signal round-trip latency, mission clocks).

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

  • Public Engagement & Scientific Outreach: Bridges complex planetary science, aerospace engineering, and public curiosity by making historical spacecraft telemetry accessible and visually engaging.
  • Interactive STEM Education: Helps students, educators, and space enthusiasts understand the harsh operational constraints of Mars (dust obscuration on solar panels, signal latency, RTG decay, thin atmospheric dynamics).
  • Mission Planning Prototype: Demonstrates how multi-factor landing site analytics (LSI) can aid in evaluating future human and robotic exploration zones.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

  • Languages: TypeScript 5 (Strict mode enforced, zero-any policy), JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, SQL.
    • Next.js 14 (App Router) & React 18
    • Tailwind CSS, PostCSS, Autoprefixer, clsx, tailwind-merge
    • Lucide React (Aerospace telemetry iconography)
    • Three.js, @react-three/fiber, @react-three/drei
    • GSAP (GreenSock) & ScrollTrigger
    • Lenis (Smooth scroll normalization)
    • Framer Motion
    • Node.js & Fastify v5
    • better-sqlite3 (SQLite embedded engine with parameterized queries)
    • Zod (End-to-end schema validation)
    • JSON Web Tokens (JWT) with RS256 asymmetric keys & secure HTTP-only cookies
    • @fastify/rate-limit & @fastify/cors

5. How is your project creative?

  • Cinematic Mission Control Aesthetic: Rather than presenting scientific data as dry spreadsheets, the UI mimics an authentic deep-space ground operations center featuring dark aerospace glassmorphism, glowing status lamps, custom magnetic cursor interactions, and mission clocks measured in Sols.
  • Dual 3D Exploration Modalities: Blends planetary-scale orbit navigation (interactive 3D Mars globe with landing coordinate markers) with micro-scale vehicle inspection (interactive 3D rover models).
  • Storytelling Through Data: Each vehicle profile includes historical facts, power degradation records (e.g., dust accumulation on Opportunity, broken rotor blades on Ingenuity, silent drift on Pioneer), and Deep Space Network (DSN) signal propagation latency.

6. What factors did your team consider?

  1. Network Reliability & NASA API Constraints: NASA endpoints enforce strict rate limits; the team implemented automatic fallback caching and simulated fallback feeds (meta.source: "mock") to prevent black screens.
    • Enforced strict Zod validation on all payload requests.
    • Parameterized queries on SQLite to eliminate SQL injection.
    • HTTP-only, sameSite: 'lax' cookie policies and restrictive CORS rules.
  2. Physical & Environmental Accuracy: Incorporating real Martian environmental factors—atmospheric density, pressure, temperature swings, solar array dust obscuration, and orbital mechanics.
